title: DOJ Appoints Special Counsel Jack Smith
description_short: Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Jack Smith as special counsel to oversee investigations into Trump.
description_medium: Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Jack Smith as special counsel in November 2022 to oversee federal investigations into efforts to overturn the 2020 election and the handling of classified records at Mar-a-Lago. Garland said Smith could continue both investigations and prosecute federal crimes arising from them. The supplied announcement transcript does not include the appointment order’s detailed oversight and reporting terms.
description_long: Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Jack Smith as special counsel on November 18, 2022. The Justice Department announcement described two assignments: the investigation into possible unlawful interference with the transfer of power after the 2020 election, including the January 6 certification, and the investigation into classified records removed from the White House and possible obstruction at Mar-a-Lago. Garland said Smith could continue both inquiries and prosecute federal crimes arising from them, exercising independent prosecutorial judgment. The announcement established the special counsel and the broad subjects of his work. The linked Justice Department press-release address is no longer available, though the supplied official video transcript preserves the announcement. That transcript does not include the full written appointment order or its detailed oversight and reporting provisions. Those terms govern the counsel’s relationship with the attorney general and what is made public, so they cannot be inferred from the announcement alone.

preserved_fields.title: DOJ Appoints Special Counsel Jack Smith
preserved_fields.description_short: Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Jack Smith as special counsel to oversee investigations into Trump.

notes: Needs context: the announcement identifies the two investigations and prosecution authority, but the linked written order is unavailable in the supplied material. Missing: the order’s supervision, oversight, and reporting terms. Proposed correction: describe the appointment and stated scope only unless the written order is recovered.

title: David Shulkin VA Secretary — Used Government Money for European Trip With Wife
description_short: David Shulkin VA Secretary — Used Government Money for European Trip With Wife
description_medium: A VA inspector general investigation found that Secretary David Shulkin’s 11-day July 2017 Europe trip cost the department at least $122,334 and included significant time for preplanned tourism. The report found that altered documentation led to approval of his wife as an invitational traveler, with $4,312 paid for her airfare, and that Shulkin improperly accepted Wimbledon tickets and hospitality. The trip total was not the amount spent on his wife.
description_long: The Department of Veterans Affairs inspector general investigated Secretary David Shulkin’s July 2017 trip to Europe after an anonymous complaint alleged that an official visit included more personal activity than government work. The 11-day trip included a day and a half of meetings with Danish veterans’ health officials and experts, a London summit, and significant time for preplanned tourist activities. The VA OIG reported that the trip cost the department at least $122,334. It found that the chief of staff altered a document and misrepresented information to ethics officials, leading to approval of Shulkin’s wife as an “invitational traveler.” VA paid $4,312 for her airfare; the report says that was the only travel cost claimed for her. The inspector general also found that Shulkin improperly accepted Wimbledon tickets and related hospitality, and that a VA employee’s time was used to arrange tourism. The report made five recommendations, including reimbursement of the airfare and ticket-related benefits. It listed zero questioned costs and did not determine whether the trip was essential, so the full trip cost should not be described as an improper payment.

preserved_fields.title: David Shulkin VA Secretary — Used Government Money for European Trip With Wife
preserved_fields.description_short: David Shulkin VA Secretary — Used Government Money for European Trip With Wife

notes: Complete from the linked VA OIG report. It distinguishes the $122,334 full-trip cost from $4,312 in airfare paid for Shulkin’s wife; the report lists $0 questioned costs and says it did not assess whether the trip was essential.

title: ICE Buys $20M Shock Gloves for Immigration Enforcement
description_short: ICE Buys $20M Shock Gloves for Immigration Enforcement
description_medium: ICE announced plans in August 2026 to spend up to $20 million on gloves that deliver an electric shock. The agency said the devices could reduce reliance on firearms and pepper spray and identified limits on their use. New York officials and Representative Pramila Jayapal criticized the plan. A 2024 death after shocks from a glove and a Taser occurred in a Kentucky detention center, not in ICE custody.
description_long: Immigration and Customs Enforcement announced plans in August 2026 to spend up to $20 million on gloves that deliver an electric shock, according to a published contract described by JURIST. The manufacturer, Compliant Technologies, calls them “conductive distraction and de-escalation devices”; the product is also known as a GLOVE or “zap glove.” ICE said the equipment could reduce the need for firearms and pepper spray and said officers would not use it on certain high-risk people, including pregnant women. New York Attorney General Letitia James, Governor Kathy Hochul, and Representative Pramila Jayapal criticized the proposal as a civil-rights concern or a dangerous addition to ICE’s enforcement tools. JURIST also reported that Jonathan Mansfield died after receiving 27 shocks from a GLOVE and 13 from a Taser at a Kentucky detention center in 2024; two glove shocks lasted far beyond the manufacturer’s recommended maximum. That incident involved another agency and setting, so it does not establish ICE use or injury. The purchase was described as a plan, and the supplied report does not establish deployment totals or final operating rules.

preserved_fields.title: ICE Buys $20M Shock Gloves for Immigration Enforcement
preserved_fields.description_short: ICE Buys $20M Shock Gloves for Immigration Enforcement

notes: Complete from the supplied account and focused reading of JURIST. The ICE purchase is a plan; the cited 2024 death occurred in a Kentucky detention center under another agency and is not presented as an ICE incident.

title: Trump sued over Truth Social API charging $100K for early post access

The supplied synopsis says the plaintiffs allege the practice is unfair and potentially illegal. description_long: A Fox News headline reports a lawsuit concerning Truth Social’s API and an asserted $100,000 charge for early access to posts. title: Trump Investigations Ongoing
description_medium: CBS News’s “Trump Investigations” page is a rolling collection of dated coverage, not a single status report. It lists matters at different stages, including the 2025 firing of Justice Department employees tied to Jack Smith’s probes, appeals in New York cases, and rulings affecting the Mar-a-Lago documents case. It does not identify a fixed date or provide a complete inventory of investigations still open.
description_long: CBS News’s “Trump Investigations” feature collects dated reports about criminal, civil, and oversight proceedings involving Donald Trump. The page includes coverage of about a dozen Justice Department employees tied to Jack Smith’s probes being fired in January 2025, the appeals and rulings in New York civil cases, the 2025 dismissal of charges against two co-defendants in the classified-documents case, and a judge’s later decision blocking release of Smith’s report on that case. These entries describe separate proceedings at different stages; they do not show that every investigation remains open or that all were conducted by the same agencies. The page is updated as new stories appear and does not provide a cutoff date, a complete list of investigations, or a consolidated status for each one. The generic title “Trump Investigations Ongoing” therefore needs a specific date and proceeding to support its claim. A case-by-case account should identify the conduct, investigating body, and current court or agency status rather than treating this rolling feature as a definitive register.
notes: Needs context: the linked CBS page is a rolling collection, not a dated case inventory. Missing: the particular proceeding, cutoff date, responsible body, and status supporting the title’s claim that investigations are ongoing.
